Class OffscreenSimpleFactory

java.lang.Object
com.cleanroommc.modularui.factory.AbstractUIFactory<com.cleanroommc.modularui.factory.GuiData>
com.cleanroommc.modularui.factory.SimpleGuiFactory
com.sbancuz.offscreen.integration.mui2.OffscreenSimpleFactory
All Implemented Interfaces:
com.cleanroommc.modularui.api.UIFactory<com.cleanroommc.modularui.factory.GuiData>
public class OffscreenSimpleFactory extends com.cleanroommc.modularui.factory.SimpleGuiFactory
A SimpleGuiFactory that opens a server-synchronized GUI in a desktop window.

Construct the same named factory during common initialization on both client and server. Its constructor registers it with ModularUI. The panel builder runs on both sides: create the same sync-handler layout and keep client-only drawing classes out of the common builder path. Call openOffscreen() on the client thread with a world and player available. The returned window shows local waiting feedback while the server's answer is in flight; use OffscreenAPI.isReady(Window) to check readiness.

For a complete registration and opening example, follow the factory creation walkthrough.

Minecraft still owns one active slot container per player. Opening another synchronized offscreen factory closes an existing session; it does not create independent server inventories for every desktop window. Use OffscreenAPI.close(Window) for ordinary closure and the session will handle the handshake. A request identifier carried in GuiData separates late replies from newer opens.

    • OffscreenSimpleFactory

      public OffscreenSimpleFactory(String name, String modId, OffscreenSimpleFactory.PanelBuilder builder)
      Registers a named factory through ModularUI's SimpleGuiFactory constructor.
      Parameters:
      name - factory name of at most 32 characters, identical on both sides and unique to this registration
      modId - owning mod ID used when creating the client screen
      builder - common-side panel/sync-handler builder
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the name exceeds 32 characters or is already registered with ModularUI

  • Method Details

    • openOffscreen

      @Nullable public Window openOffscreen()
      Requests a synchronized screen and returns its window without blocking for the reply. Repeating the same factory's in-flight open returns that pending window. Another factory's pending request prevents a new open until it resolves.
      Returns:
      created or already pending window, or null if the world or player is missing, another factory is opening, or native setup cannot retain a window
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if native window creation fails

    • openOffscreen

      @Nullable public Window openOffscreen(@Nullable WindowChrome chrome)
      Opens the synchronized panel with optional custom chrome from native creation onward. A repeated in-flight open returns its existing window without changing that window's appearance. Requests made inside a hosted screen callback retain a frozen image of that screen with a loading spinner until the server screen attaches.
      Parameters:
      chrome - custom title bar, or null to keep native Windows/OS chrome
      Returns:
      pending/new native owner, or null when another factory is pending or no player exists

    • openAnimated

      @Nullable public Window openAnimated(@Nullable WindowChrome chrome, @Nullable Timeline entrance, @Nullable Timeline exit)
      Configures visual entrance and exit before showing a synchronized window. Entrance begins while the local waiting screen is visible; it does not indicate server readiness. Existing pending windows are returned unchanged.
      Parameters:
      chrome - custom caption, or null for native chrome
      entrance - finite entrance plan, or null
      exit - finite visual exit plan, or null
      Returns:
      pending/new window, or null when a competing request or absent player prevents opening

    • toggleOffscreen

      @Nullable public Window toggleOffscreen()
      Closes this factory's active screen, or opens one if it has no active session.

      If the session is still waiting for the server's panel, returns that pending window instead of closing it. Opening follows the same rules as openOffscreen(), including null results and propagated exceptions.

      Returns:
      pending or newly opened window, or null after closure or an unsuccessful open
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if opening a new native window fails
